 Austin Reaves, Quentin Grimes, Matisse Thybulle, Jake LaRavia and Walker Kessler will start Wednesday’s game against the Clippers. 
 Luka Dončić and Ziaire Williams will miss Wednesday’s game, the Lakers’ second in as many nights. Grimes and LaRavia will replace them in the lineup, which also means Austin Reaves will take on the primary playmaking responsibilities for the starters. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Luka Dončić 
 LAL 
 Forward-Guard 
 #77 
 Personalize your Rotoworld feed by favoriting players 
 Luka Dončić (back) has been ruled out against the Clippers on Wednesday. 
 Dončić will miss the second leg of the Lakers’ back-to-back, which means Austin Reaves should be the focal point of the offense. Quentin Grimes or Collin Sexton will likely replace Dončić in the starting unit, with both taking on extended roles. 
 Jake LaRavia 
 LAL 
 Forward 
 #12 
 Jake LaRavia (ankle) is off the injury report vs. Jazz. 
 LaRavia did not play on Friday against the Clippers, but was removed off the injury report ahead of Sunday’s tilt against the Jazz. The forward scored 10 points in 18 minutes of action in the Lakers season opener against the Warriors. 
 Jake LaRavia 
 LAL 
 Forward 
 #12 
 Jake LaRavia (ankle) is out for Friday’s game against the Clippers. 
 LaRavia was initially listed as questionable, but it should be no surprise that he’s been ruled out Friday after he sprained his right ankle in Wednesday’s win over the Warriors. The good news is that the injury isn’t considered serious and he should return to game action soon. Without LaRavia, Quentin Grimes could see enough minutes off the bench to be worth steaming consideration in category leagues. 
 Jake LaRavia 
 LAL 
 Forward 
 #12 
 Jake LaRavia (ankle) is questionable for Friday’s game against the Clippers. 
 LaRavia sprained his right ankle in Wednesday’s win over the Warriors, and team trainers helped him back to the locker room. With Cameron Carr (oblique) and Adou Thiero (knee) already out, LaRavia’s minutes will likely be split among Matisse Thybulle, Ziaire Williams and Quentin Grimes if he can’t play on Friday. Despite coming off the bench, Grimes offers a higher category league ceiling than Thybulle or Williams. 
 Jake LaRavia 
 LAL 
 Forward 
 #12 
 Jake LaRavia (ankle) was helped to the locker room and will not return against Warriors. 
 Jake was on the floor in pain and went to the locker room. We’ll likely get an update tomorrow, but the Lakers didn’t have Adou Thiero, Cameron Carr, or Collin Sexton on Wednesday. Jarred Vanderbilt should be the biggest beneficiary if LaRavia misses time and Thiero is still out. We might see more Ziaire Williams and Matisse Thybulle as well. 
 Collin Sexton 
 LAL 
 Guard 
 #10 
 Collin Sexton (leg) will miss Wednesday’s season opener against the Warriors. 
 Sexton missed the preseason, and his Lakers debut will have to wait while he recovers from a right soleus strain. In Sexton’s absence, more minutes could be available for Ziaire Williams, Quentin Grimes and Bronny James. 
 Quentin Grimes 
 LAL 
 Guard 
 #5 
 Quentin Grimes tallied 11 points (4-of-9 FGs), two rebounds, three assists and three three-pointers in Friday’s exhibition against the Nuggets. 
 Grimes, a starter for most of the preseason, came off the bench in Friday’s finale. That may be the role he’s expected to fill, especially as the Lakers await Collin Sexton’s return from injury. The second unit needs a perimeter player who can create offensively, even if the Lakers can stagger the minutes of stars Luka Dončić and Austin Reaves. Grimes can provide scoring, making him a worthwhile pick in later rounds. 
 Jake LaRavia 
 LAL 
 Forward 
 #12 
 Jake LaRavia tallied 12 points (5-of-6 FGs, 0-of-3 FTs), three rebounds, two assists, two steals, two blocks and two three-pointers in Monday’s exhibition against the Kings. 
 With LeBron James and Rui Hachimura out of the picture, LaRavia’s opportunities should increase, whether he starts or comes off the bench. He was the Lakers’ sixth man on Monday and provided solid production outside of his poor foul shooting. While he may not be someone who fantasy managers look to invest a top-100 pick in, LaRavia is well worth the risk as a late-round option. 
 Quentin Grimes 
 LAL 
 Guard 
 #5 
 Quentin Grimes accounted for 16 points (5-of-7 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), one assist and two three-pointers in Monday’s exhibition against the Kings. 
 Going into training camp, many saw Grimes as a frontrunner for one of the two undecided spots in the Lakers’ starting lineup. He started Monday’s preseason opener, logging 19 minutes and shooting reliably alongside playmaker Luka Dončić. The concern is that Grimes offered little production beyond points, three-pointers and percentages. Hopefully, that won’t be the case for him once the games count. 
 Quentin Grimes 
 LAL 
 Guard 
 #5 
 Quentin Grimes agreed to a four-year, $60 million contract with the Lakers, according to ESPN’s Shams Charania. 
 Grimes turned 26 in May. A five-year NBA veteran, the former first-round pick by the Clippers in the 2021 NBA Draft has been traded four times in his career including on draft night. Grimes spent last season with the 76ers, appearing in 75 games and starting 19 of them. He averaged 13.4 points. Grimes fits the Lakers as an aggressive scorer off the bench.

 Trevon Brazile accounted for 11 points (5-of-9 FGs), eight rebounds, one steal, one block and one three-pointer in Wednesday’s win over the Pelicans.
 After performing well coming off the bench in Denver’s first three games, Brazile made his first NBA start on Wednesday. The rookie forward played 32 minutes against the Pelicans and had another productive outing. The Nuggets needed more athleticism in their rotation, especially after losing Peyton Watson, and Brazile fits the bill. He isn’t a must-roster player in 12-team leagues, but the rookie should be rostered in deeper redraft leagues, even if he doesn’t stick in the starting lineup. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Ajay Mitchell had 29 points (12-of-20 FGs, 3-of-3 FTs), four rebounds, three assists, two steals, one block and two three-pointers in Wednesday’s game against the Mavericks. 
 Mitchell moved into the starting lineup Monday with the Thunder dealing with a number of injuries and dropped a career-high 30 points in the win over the Suns. He scored 29 points Wednesday against the Mavericks, though it still wasn’t enough to prevent a blowout loss. Nevertheless, Mitchell has become a must-roster player and potentially a league-winner as he continues to produce at a high level when given increased opportunities. 
 -  Nick Shlain

 Washington has now had at least 18 points, at least nine rebounds, at least two three-pointers and at least one block in three of his last four games. He’ll easily pay off his draft cost if he keeps up this level of production.

 Cooper Flagg had 26 points (10-of-23 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), five rebounds, eight assists and two three-pointers in Wednesday’s 120-96 victory over the Thunder. 
 Flagg is averaging 25.3 points, 6.8 assists, 5.3 rebounds, 2.8 steals and 1.3 blocks through four games this year. The 19-year-old’s game Wednesday against the Thunder was even more impressive considering he also had zero turnovers. Easily the best young player in the league, Flagg may already have elevated himself into being part of the MVP conversation.

 Stephon Castle

 #5 
 Player Stats

 Stephon Castle put up 14 points (6-of-13 FGs, 1-of-2 FTs), six rebounds, eight assists, two steals, a block, and a three in win against the Jazz. 
 Castle’s ability to put up peripheral stats will be an important part of his fantasy outlook in dynasty leagues. The main thing that is notable at this point is that he has attempted 8.2 3PT attempts per game this season which is up from 3.6 last season. In the present, if you drafted him, you’d be feeling pretty happy with the start he has had this season. He’s gotten you points, rebounds, and assists on a consistent basis. If he is shooting 3’s on a consistent basis, he could be a fantasy monster and a staple in the top 50 for years to come.

 Dylan Harper put up 13 points (4-of-17 FGs, 3-of-3 FTs), five rebounds, eight assists, two steals, and two 3-pointers on Wednesday. 
 This game had the outline of a monster fantasy performance with the rebounds and assists. Unfortunately he shot 4-17 from the field which puts a dampener on everything else. Once he becomes the established guy, he will be an absolute monster in fantasy. His ability to get to the rim at will is going to be one of the best in the league when he’s at his peak.

 Devin Vassell with 21 points (8-of-18 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), five rebounds, two assists, three steals and a three against the Jazz. 
 Vassell made some big shots in the fourth quarter to keep the Spurs in this game. While it was a good performance, he’s only up to 12.6 points, 4 rebounds, and 3.8 assists on the season. He’s a points and 3-point streamer who will occasionally have good games but is not a must in most redraft leagues. There’s too many high usage players on the team for him to be able to score like this consistently.

 Victor Wembanyama had 36 points (14-of-25 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), 14 rebounds, five assists, two steals, two blocks and four 3-pointers in the 117-111 overtime win against the Jazz. 
 Wembanyama took advantage of the mediocre Jazz defense and got whatever he wanted in this game. His defensive presence changes how offenses attack the rim. He has been exactly what you wanted if you drafted him with the first pick in redraft leagues. Its hard to complain and you hope he doesn’t get hurt if you have him.

 Jalen Smith finished Wednesday’s loss to the Knicks with 17 points (7-of-12 FGs), 11 rebounds, five assists, three blocks and three three-pointers.
 While the Bulls await Nic Claxton’s return from a strained hamstring, Smith continues to provide reliable fantasy value. He finished Wednesday’s loss with his second double-double of the season and provided solid value in assists, blocks, and three-pointers. Smith is rostered in 46 percent of Yahoo leagues; managers needing a center for Friday’s 10-game slate should make sure he isn’t sitting on the waiver wire.
